sentences.show: In 1934, the most wanted man in America broke out of an escape-proof jail. With a gun he may have carved from wood.
His name was John Dillinger. Accused of robbing 24 banks.
In January he was caught, and locked up in Crown Point, Indiana.
The police told the newspapers it was escape-proof. They even posted extra guards.
On 3 March, during morning exercise, Dillinger pulled out a pistol.
He took hostages, locked up the guards, and walked out, without firing a single shot.
Then he drove away in the sheriff's own car.
But was the gun even real? FBI files say he carved it out of wood, with a razor blade.
A deputy swore it was real. His lawyer's investigator claimed he had smuggled it in himself. Nobody agrees, to this day.
That stolen car crossed a state line. Now J. Edgar Hoover's agents hunted him as Public Enemy No. 1.
Dillinger paid for plastic surgery, and tried to burn off his fingerprints with acid.
It wasn't enough. In July, a brothel owner, Anna Sage, tipped off the FBI, to save herself from deportation.
He walked out of the Biograph Theater in Chicago. Agents were waiting. He ran for the alley, and was shot dead.
Crowds dipped handkerchiefs in his blood. And the gun from Crown Point? Real steel, or wood?
Dillinger broke out of Crown Point. Break out of the scroll, and subscribe.
